title: Failed Edits never reach the gate
mechanism: 'String to replace not found in file' is a validation rejection that Claude Code returns before any hook runs, so neither PreToolUse nor PostToolUseFailure fires for a failing Edit; hdc_hooks.py claims to cover 'all tools'.
consequence: The most common Edit retry loop is invisible to both the gate and the reminder.
severity: not stated per finding; verdict lists it under 'misses the loops it targets' (later accepted as a documented gap in round 2)

title: A failed Bash command reported as success clears the failure count
mechanism: Two routes deliver a failed command to PostToolUse instead of PostToolUseFailure, where mode_success deletes the call's failure count: exit-code interpretation (grep exit 1 arrives with returnCodeInterpretation 'No matches found') and pipelines whose last command exits 0 (pytest 2>&1 | tail -30). The README's stated blind spot ('a wrong answer with exit code 0') understates this.
consequence: The gate never arms for piped test runs and each run resets the count; README.md:45 understates the gap.
severity: not stated per finding; verdict lists it under 'misses the loops it targets' and requires correcting README.md:45-46 (later accepted as a documented gap in round 2)
how_found: ran (grep routing, pipe exit status); reasoned (piped failure routed to PostToolUse)

title: Subagents share the parent session's state file and edit epoch
mechanism: Subagent payloads carry the parent's session_id and scratchpad_dir (only agent_id differs), and hdc_hooks.py:107-111 keys the state file by session only, so every agent reads and writes one state file and one edit epoch.
consequence: A subagent is denied a call it never made with a false 'has failed 2 times' message, any agent's edit reopens every agent's gate, and a lost epoch update blocks all agents.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 1
how_found: ran (real session: subagent's first false denied after parent's two)

title: Concurrent hooks lose updates and can corrupt the state file
mechanism: load_state -> modify -> save_state (hdc_hooks.py:114-135) runs with no lock, and every writer uses the same temporary path path+'.tmp'; PostToolUse fires concurrently for parallel tool calls and subagents add writers.
consequence: In 40 trials of 13 parallel hooks the Edit epoch bump was lost 3 times, the file was left as invalid JSON once, and a failure count was lost 39 times, so the gate denies after a real edit or arms late or never.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 1

title: A fix that changes only whitespace is denied as unchanged
mechanism: canonical_call (hdc_hooks.py:73-76) collapses runs of whitespace inside every string before hashing, so a re-indented heredoc or printf format hashes identically to the failed call.
consequence: A correct whitespace-only fix (e.g. fixing an IndentationError in a heredoc) is denied as an identical retry.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 2

title: Reminder fires on any two Bash failures, claiming 'the same signature'
mechanism: normalise_error (hdc_hooks.py:49) keeps only the first line of the error; for Bash that is always 'Exit code N', which normalises to 'exit code <n>', so every Bash failure in a session shares one signature.
consequence: The second unrelated Bash failure triggers a reminder with a false 'same signature' claim (ls on a missing dir reported as occurrence 3 after two false runs).
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 3

title: Unexpected tool_input fields: the ignore list is wrong in both directions
mechanism: IGNORED_INPUT_FIELDS (hdc_hooks.py:64) lists fields to ignore rather than fields to key on: unlisted extra fields (dangerouslyDisableSandbox, a trailing shell comment in command) make a denied call pass, while timeout and run_in_background are ignored although they really change the call (test/run_tests.sh:33-34 asserts a larger timeout is denied). Any future per-call field silently disables the gate.
consequence: The gate is trivially evaded by an extra field or comment, and a correct retry with a larger timeout is wrongly denied.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 2
how_found: ran (extra fields pass; run_in_background/timeout denied); reasoned (future fields)

title: The tests don't exercise real payloads
mechanism: test/run_tests.sh fixtures are hand-written (the Edit fixture uses old_str/new_str where the real tool uses old_string/new_string), no fixture was captured from a real session (breaking docs/CLAUDE.md:19's own rule), line 36 asserts that success mode prints nothing, which always holds, and C1-C7 have no coverage.
consequence: The suite passes 15/15 while missing every real-payload defect found this round.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 7

title: The manifest still advertises the removed Stop reviewer
mechanism: .claude-plugin/plugin.json:4 describes 'a fresh-context reviewer at Stop' while the README says it was removed and hooks/hooks.json has no Stop hook.
consequence: The manifest description is false.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 6

title: Reminder labelled 'Engineer detector, Administer nudge'; it is Administer
mechanism: README.md:8 labels the reminder Engineer, but its only output is additionalContext the model must read and act on; nothing is caught or stopped, and because of C6 the 'detector' reports repeats that aren't repeats.
consequence: The component carries a rung label the framework's own test does not support.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 6

title: Gate labelled Engineer: right for the block, but scope and claims overstated
mechanism: README.md:7,46 and docs/CLAUDE.md:29 claim the gate 'cannot be talked past, only edited past' and has false positives 'close to the definition of the loop'; a trailing shell comment gets past it (C7), the deny message (hdc_hooks.py:236-238) tells the model to 'vary the call', any edit to any file (including the NOTES.md line docs/CLAUDE.md:31 asks for) reopens it, and the deny message's 'name the rung'/'say so to the user' instructions depend on model compliance (Administer).
consequence: The docs overstate the gate's scope and mislabel its instructions; the correct label is 'Engineer, narrow: identical failing Bash and MCP retries', with the message instructions labelled Administer.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 6

title: PostToolUse bookkeeping labelled 'support'; it is part of the gate
mechanism: README.md:9 calls the PostToolUse bookkeeping 'support', but it decides when the gate reopens, so its defects (clearing counts on interpreted exits C2, losing epoch updates C4, recognising only four edit tools H4) are gate defects kept out of the gate's description.
consequence: The gate's description omits the failure modes of the component that controls reopening.

title: 'Resolving to be more careful' is given two different rungs
mechanism: hdc_hooks.py:151 (injected reminder), SKILL.md:27 and docs/hierarchy-of-defect-controls.md:86 call it Protect; docs/CLAUDE.md:25 calls it Administer. Root cause: the framework doc lists 'Be careful' comments under Protect (line 62) against its own definitions; the correct rung is Administer.
consequence: The plugin's own injected text gives the model the wrong rung label.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 6

title: Transient network error: third identical run denied; deny message teaches cosmetic evasion
mechanism: npm install fails twice with ETIMEDOUT and the third identical run is denied; the gate arms on the call alone without checking that the error signature matches, and the deny message recommends varying the call, which a comment satisfies, while 'say so to the user' is never enforced.
consequence: A legitimate retry is denied and the escape hatch trains the model to evade with cosmetic changes.

title: Success depends on external state: user fixes outside the session cannot reopen the gate
mechanism: The gate reopens only on an edit-tool write; when the user acted outside the session ('I restarted Postgres, try again') nothing changes the epoch, and the deny message's 'no file has been edited' is irrelevant. Polling with sleep is a different call so that case escapes.
consequence: A retry after an external fix is wrongly denied; proposed fix is clearing counts on UserPromptSubmit.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 4

title: File changed by a tool not in EDIT_TOOLS does not reopen the gate
mechanism: Only the four tools in EDIT_TOOLS bump the edit epoch; a fix applied by sed -i, git apply, eslint --fix, a generator script or the user's IDE leaves the epoch unchanged, so the gate stays closed and the message 'no file has been edited since the last failure' is false.
consequence: The model is told its fix didn't take; proposed replacement is a working-tree fingerprint (git status + diff).
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 5

title: MCP tools that write files are not recognised as edits; README asks the installer to add them
mechanism: Filesystem/JetBrains-style MCP servers write files outside EDIT_TOOLS; README.md:39 asks the installer to add tool names to EDIT_TOOLS, which is itself an Administer control.
consequence: Fixes applied through MCP file servers do not reopen the gate and the mitigation depends on a human remembering to configure it.
severity: not stated per finding; 'Required before release' item 5

title: The gap left by the removed Stop reviewer: silent no-op in-place edits are undetected
mechanism: docs/CLAUDE.md:29 names 'a replacement that matched nothing reports success' as the silent repeat, but nothing in the package detects it after the Stop reviewer was removed; the review proposes a deterministic no-op in-place edit detector (sed -i/perl -pi/git apply fingerprint before/after, recorded as a failure).
consequence: A successful-looking sed/patch that changed nothing is neither recorded nor gated.
severity: not stated ('the gap is still open')

title: Porcelain git diff takes index.lock and makes concurrent git writes fail
mechanism: tree_fingerprint (hdc_hooks.py:178) runs porcelain 'git diff --no-color' on every gate, success and failure hook; that command refreshes the index and takes .git/index.lock even with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, so a concurrent git add/commit (parallel call, subagent, IDE, user) fails with 'Unable to create .git/index.lock'. Fix proposed: git diff-files -p / git diff-index -p --cached HEAD under GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, handling unborn HEAD (reasoned caveat).
consequence: 38/400 of the user's own commits failed on index.lock (15/400 with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0; 0 control), breaking work outside the hook's scope despite the docstring's 'never break a session' promise.

title: No-op detector reports real edits as 'the replacement matched nothing'
mechanism: hdc_hooks.py:370-384 compares the repo tree fingerprint before and after any command matching INPLACE_EDIT_RE; an in-place edit whose effect is outside the fingerprint (gitignored .env, out-of-repo file, 'sed -i ... && git commit' leaving the tree clean, 'git apply --check' dry run) is recorded as a failure.
consequence: The model is told a successful edit did nothing and may redo or undo it; the false failure counts toward a denial.

title: Fingerprint omits HEAD, ignored files and out-of-repo files, so real fixes don't reopen the gate
mechanism: When git is available current_marker (hdc_hooks.py:157-191) is only a hash of git status plus diffs: every clean tree hashes to the empty-input SHA-1, so git checkout/pull/reset/stash pop onto a clean tree leaves the marker unchanged, and the edit counter is ignored so an Edit/Write to a gitignored or out-of-repo file no longer reopens the gate (a regression from v0.1.0).
consequence: After an Edit to gitignored .env or a git checkout to a fixing branch, the retry is denied with 'working tree is unchanged' although the command now exits 0.

title: Environment changes via Bash never reopen the gate (gap to document)
mechanism: pip install, docker start, export and similar change none of fingerprint, HEAD or edit_epoch, so after the R3 fix the only way out is a new user message; the README 'Known gaps' did not state this.
consequence: A retry after an environment fix is denied until a new user message; in -p and subagents only a real input change works.

title: Every tool call pays for two fingerprints, run one at a time under the session lock
mechanism: The gate (hdc_hooks.py:305) and success (hdc_hooks.py:365) hooks compute the git fingerprint unconditionally, including for Read/Grep/Glob, while holding the flock, so parallel tool calls queue behind one another; worst case of four git calls at GIT_TIMEOUT=3 (~12 s) exceeds the 10 s hook timeout and a killed hook loses its bookkeeping.
consequence: About +1.3 s per call and 3.2 s for six parallel gates on a 120k-file repo.

title: Error signatures still collide for test runners and commands with no output
mechanism: The signature (hdc_hooks.py:97-104) is 'exit N:' plus the first non-empty output line; pytest's first line is always the '==== test session starts ====' banner, and every failing command with no output (false, test -f, cmp -s) gets just 'exit N:'. The package test (run_tests.py:161-164) only uses first lines that already differ.
consequence: Two different failing pytest commands trigger a false 'same signature' reminder.
how_found: ran (two pytest commands); real session (false recorded as 'exit 1:')

title: A per-run id in the error stops the gate from ever arming
mechanism: normalise_line (hdc_hooks.py:75-85) only normalises all-digit tokens; hex ids, request ids, UUIDs and container ids differ between runs so each failure looks new and the count resets to 1 (hdc_hooks.py:287).
consequence: ./deploy.sh failed four times with different hex request ids and the gate allowed all four (fails open).

title: Test coverage misses the new failure modes
mechanism: The concurrency test (run_tests.py:216-233) uses a non-git directory so the fingerprint+lock path is never tested under contention; there are no tests for gitignored/out-of-repo files, HEAD moves, compound commands, dry-run flags, lock contention with a concurrent git write, or the pytest banner signature.
consequence: The suite passes 22/22 while R1-R6 are all present.

title: No-op detector's 'Engineer, narrow' label is half right
mechanism: README.md:8: recording the no-op as a failure is deterministic and arms the gate against identical retries (Engineer), but the targeted defect, the model proceeding as if the replacement happened, is countered only by an additionalContext message the model must read (Administer). Correction to round 1, which said the detector closed the gap.
consequence: Correct label is 'Engineer for the identical-retry loop; Administer for the silent no-op itself'.

title: Gate scope overstated: 'a fix applied by sed, a generator, an MCP file server, or the user's IDE reopens the gate'
mechanism: README.md:35 and the docstring (hdc_hooks.py:31-35) claim any such fix reopens the gate; per R3 this is true only for tracked or non-ignored files inside the repo, and not for HEAD moves or environment changes.
consequence: The docs promise reopening in cases where the gate stays closed.

title: Package discloses that it breaks its own real-payload rule (fixtures reconstructed, not captured)
mechanism: docs/CLAUDE.md:19 requires every hook to be exercised against a real payload; README.md:29 and run_tests.py:5-12 say the fixtures are 'reconstructed, not captured'. The disclosure is a note (Administer) standing in for an unmet check. Round 3 supplied six captured payloads; closed in v0.4.0.
consequence: No test runs against a captured payload per event.

title: test_documented_gaps is documentation dressed as a test
mechanism: run_tests.py:291-303 asserts the length of a literal list, so it cannot fail, yet counts toward the '22 tests' at README.md:27; this is the pattern docs/CLAUDE.md:18 warns about (looks like a control, only states things).
consequence: The test count is inflated by a test that checks nothing.

title: Reminder asserts 'the previous remedy was too low on the ladder', which the hook cannot know
mechanism: The reminder text at hdc_hooks.py:272 states the previous remedy was too low; on deliberate or user-requested failures there was no remedy, and in the resumed real turn the model spent its reply rebutting the claim.
consequence: Administer noise and a false statement on intentional failures; later rounds record the model arguing with the hook as 'accepted by design'.
severity: should fix (harm table item 7); not applicable/Administer noise

title: Perl switches containing 'i' are treated as in-place edits
mechanism: In-place detection at hdc_hooks.py:189-195 is '"i" in t[1:]' for any short-option token, so -Ilib, -Mstrict, -MList::Util=sum and -MFile::Spec count as in-place; operand files are hashed, found unchanged, and the read-only command is recorded as a failure.
consequence: perl -c -Ilib lib/Foo.pm is reported as 'the replacement matched nothing' on each run and denied on the third.

title: patch / git apply outside git, or to gitignored files, reported as no-ops
mechanism: For git apply and patch the tree plan (hdc_hooks.py:206-209, 466-467) compares the marker before and after; outside git the marker is 'nogit:e<epoch>', identical unless an Edit tool ran (v0.2.0's before.startswith('git:') guard was dropped), and inside git a gitignored target does not change the tree fingerprint.
consequence: A real patch -p1 or git apply outside a repo, or to .env, is reported as 'target is byte-identical ... matched nothing' and counts toward a denial.

title: Error signatures still collide for Python tracebacks and pytest output (residual of R2-R5, new mechanism)
mechanism: pick_error_line/error_signature (hdc_hooks.py:101-127) use the first error-like line and DECORATION_RE excludes only all-punctuation lines, so every Python traceback yields 'Traceback (most recent call last):' and default pytest output yields the '==== FAILURES ====' banner (or the 'test session starts' banner when no line matches). The package test uses output whose first error-like line is a FAILED line.
consequence: Unrelated scripts trigger a false 'same signature' reminder, and a script whose exception changes between runs does not restart the count, so run 3 is denied although README.md:33 says the gate arms only on the same error.
how_found: ran (N3, N3b, E7, pytest sample output)

title: Compound-command check runs on the raw string, including quoted text
mechanism: COMPOUND_RE (hdc_hooks.py:73) is applied at line 180 before shlex, so a '|' or ';' inside a quoted sed script (s|a|b|, s/a/b/;s/c/d/) marks the command compound and detection is skipped.
consequence: sed -i 's|zzz|yyy|' x.txt run three times as a genuine no-op is never flagged and never blocked (fails open).

title: README.md:37 'Plumbing only' is inaccurate: git status is porcelain
mechanism: README.md:37 attributes the index-lock fix to using plumbing only, but the fingerprint runs 'git status --porcelain', a porcelain command; the 0/400 result holds because it runs under GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0.
consequence: The doc gives the wrong reason for the index-lock claim holding.

title: 'Leaving its target byte-identical' is inaccurate for git apply/patch
mechanism: README.md:8 and docs/CLAUDE.md:29 say the detector flags commands that leave their target byte-identical; true for sed/perl, but for git apply/patch the check is whole-tree (becomes accurate only once R2b hashes patch targets).
consequence: The doc describes a per-target check the patch branch does not perform.

title: Patch branch reports real patches as no-ops in six shapes; it catches almost nothing
mechanism: patch_targets/patch_plan (hdc_hooks.py:246-319) hash only paths parsed from ---/+++ headers, resolved against payload cwd, and check only working-tree content: --cached changes only the index; rename/mode/binary patches have no ---/+++ lines so the plan is {} which line 611 treats as 'always a no-op'; 'patch src/foo.c < diff' ignores the explicit operand and header basenames resolve to nonexistent files (None before and after counts as unchanged); git apply from a subdirectory resolves 'b/sub/x.txt' against cwd instead of the repo top. A re-applied patch fails (exit 1) in every form, so the branch's only true positive is an empty patch.
consequence: The model is told a successful patch did nothing and the false failure counts toward a denial (two shapes seen in the real session); recommended fix is removing git apply/patch from the detector.

title: Output with no error-like line falls back to a generic first line
mechanism: error_lines fallback (hdc_hooks.py:122) uses the first non-decoration line when nothing matches ERRORISH_RE, so truncated pytest output (--tb=no -rN style) gives two different commands the signature 'exit 1: platform linux -- python <n>.<n>.<n>, pytest-<n>.<n>.<n>'.
consequence: Unrelated commands share a reminder signature (Administer noise).

title: Docs claim a patch is flagged when 'every file it targets' is byte-identical, but the detector doesn't know the targets
mechanism: README.md:8 and docs/CLAUDE.md:29 describe per-target checking for git apply/patch; R2c shows the parser misses targets for --cached, rename, mode, binary, explicit-operand and subdirectory patches.
consequence: The doc wording does not match what the parser actually checks; the recommended R2c fix removes the claim.

title: Compiled bytecode present in the package
mechanism: scripts/__pycache__/hdc_hooks.cpython-312.pyc is shipped in the package although the hooks run hdc_hooks.py as a script and never load it; nothing excludes __pycache__/.
consequence: A stray build artifact ships with the package.

title: Stale test description in README.md:27
mechanism: README.md:27 still says the tests cover 'every row of the round-2 retest checklist' although they now cover rows from rounds 2-4.
consequence: The README misdescribes the test suite's coverage.

title: A test silently skips one check via a conditional expression
mechanism: test/run_tests.py:459 uses 'self.assertFalse(...) if rid != "c0ffee42" else None', which skips the assertion on the last iteration instead of asserting the gate is closed after failure 2.
consequence: The intended final assertion is never made.

title: Perl switch-parsing tests were deleted with the patch tests
mechanism: v0.5.0 removed test_r4_1..test_r4_4 (read-only perl -I/-M never flagged, perl -pi no-op denied, perl -i.bak) along with the patch tests; 'grep -c perl test/run_tests.py' is 0 and the count stayed 41 only because new patch tests replaced them, so perl_inplace/sed_inplace (hdc_hooks.py:186-224), the code behind R2a, have no direct test.
consequence: A later edit could reintroduce '-Ilib counts as -i' and the suite would still pass (behaviour today is correct).
how_found: ran (grep); real session confirms current behaviour

title: Durations written against their unit (5007ms) give every run a new signature
mechanism: normalise_line (hdc_hooks.py:89-101) uses \b\d+\b, which does not match digits glued to a letter, so 'timed out after 5007ms' or ping's 'time 2033ms' is kept verbatim; affects error-like lines since v0.3.0 and, new in v0.5.0, the no-error-line fallback that now appends the last non-decoration line (ping statistics).
consequence: The count restarts every run, so the gate never arms and the reminder never fires for the transient-timeout loop the gate exists for (fails open).

title: README.md:8 component table still says git apply and patch are detected
mechanism: README.md:8 says 'A simple sed -i, perl -pi, git apply or patch ... Targets are the command's operands or the paths parsed from the patch file', contradicting README.md:58,64, docs/CLAUDE.md:29 and the docstring after the patch branch was removed in v0.5.0.
consequence: The most-read doc table describes a detector branch that no longer exists.

title: README.md:27 test list still names 'dry runs'
mechanism: README.md:27 lists dry-run tests that were removed with the patch branch.
consequence: The README names tests that no longer exist.

title: test/run_tests.py:8 says test-name numbers refer to the round-2 checklist
mechanism: The module docstring says 'Numbers in test names refer to the round-2 review's retest checklist' while test names now carry r4_/r5_ prefixes from later rounds.
consequence: Stale provenance note in the test module.

title: hdc_hooks.py:37 docstring still says 'plumbing commands only'
mechanism: The script docstring claims the fingerprint uses plumbing only; git status is porcelain. README.md:37 was corrected in v0.4.0 (R3-F2a) but the docstring was not.
consequence: The docstring repeats the inaccuracy the README fixed.

title: .gitignore excludes nothing from the tgz install; README.md:64 claim unsupported
mechanism: .gitignore lists __pycache__/, but the package directory is not a git repository and the README installs via 'tar xzf', so a tarball built from the directory would include a stray __pycache__ despite README.md:64 saying it is 'excluded from the package'.
consequence: The exclusion claim is not enforced by anything in the build.

title: Dead constant COMPOUND_RE
mechanism: COMPOUND_RE (hdc_hooks.py:75) is no longer used; tokenise replaced it.
consequence: Dead code remains in the script.

title: Unused parameter sid in _patch_never_flagged
mechanism: test/run_tests.py:306 defines _patch_never_flagged(self, cwd, cmd, sid) and never uses sid.
consequence: Dead parameter in the test helper.

title: DENY_RE truncates the signature at the first '")'
mechanism: DENY_RE (hdc_hooks.py:93-94) captures (?P<sig>.*?)"\) lazily while REMINDER_RE (95-96) captures greedily, so for an error line containing a quoted call such as ValueError("bad input") or pytest's assert parse("x") == 1 the report keys the reminder under the full signature and the deny under a truncated one (hdc_report.py:157,172).
consequence: One loop is reported as two episodes of depth 1 (episodes 2, max_depth 1 instead of 1 and 2); episodes are the report's primary unit.

title: Eager 'import traceback' slows every hook invocation
mechanism: hdc_hooks.py:75 imports traceback at module level though it is used only inside the except in main() (line 649); on Python 3.14 traceback pulls in _colorize, costing 12-15 ms per invocation, two invocations per tool call.
consequence: The unarmed gate went from 39 ms (0.5.1) to 54 ms; about 30 ms per tool call on the path the package says must spawn nothing.

title: A corrupt state file is logged once per unarmed gate call, not once
mechanism: peek_state (hdc_hooks.py:429-444) logs state_corrupt, mode_gate calls it unlocked on every gate (line 534), and the fast path returns (538-539) without rewriting the file; only a locked path (State.__exit__) heals it. test_corrupt_state_is_recorded_and_healed only exercises reset, a locked path. docs/indicators.md:67 says a corrupt state file appends one JSON line.
consequence: Three unarmed Reads produced three state_corrupt records plus a fourth from the healing hook, inflating a Tier 4 count where any non-zero count is a finding; the doc's 'one line' claim is false.

title: log_event follows symlinks
mechanism: hdc_hooks.py:391 uses os.stat (follows links) and line 402 opens with O_CREAT and no O_NOFOLLOW, so an HDC_EVENTS symlink to any user-writable file is appended to and a dangling symlink has its target created.
consequence: The hook silently writes to a file nobody intended on a path the user believed was a log (user-set path, user privileges, so small risk).

title: 'The write cannot block' / stale mount claim does not hold
mechanism: docs/indicators.md:67 and hdc_hooks.py:380-383 say a FIFO or a stale mount cannot hold a hook until its timeout; O_NONBLOCK affects FIFOs and devices, not regular files, and os.stat at line 391 runs before it and blocks on a hard-mounted stale NFS path. The FIFO case is handled by the S_ISREG check.
consequence: The doc claims an immunity the code does not have (a hung filesystem can hold the hook as it can the state file).

title: 'In two of them every commit carries the trailer' understates the measurement
mechanism: docs/indicators.md:26 says two of the eight repos have the trailer on every commit; on this machine 7 of 8 do (55/55, 7/7, 2/2, 10/10, 89/89, 175/175, 21/21; the eighth is 13/48).
consequence: The sentence misstates the data and understates the conclusion it supports.

title: 'Between 2.1.270 and 2.1.289 the stored form of a deny changed' is not established
mechanism: docs/indicators.md:65 and hdc_report.py:32-33 attribute the bare-vs-wrapped deny form to a version change, but every stored deny on this machine comes from a -p session (16 bare at 2.1.270, 4 wrapped at 2.1.289); no interactive-session deny exists and intermediate versions have no deny at all, so version vs mode is not distinguished.
consequence: The doc states as fact a cause the evidence cannot separate; should say 'observed in -p sessions' (and the report could print versions seen).

title: test_off_by_default passes against a mutant that logs to a default path
mechanism: test/run_tests.py:865-869 asserts only that its own scratch path has no records; a mutant replacing os.environ.get("HDC_EVENTS") with '... or "/tmp/hdc-default-events.jsonl"' passes the whole Tier4 class, so the docs/plugin.md:37 claim 'the Tier 4 log is off by default' is unprotected.
consequence: A regression that writes a log when HDC_EVENTS is unset would not be caught.

title: FIFO test cannot tell O_NONBLOCK from the S_ISREG check
mechanism: test_fifo_target_never_blocks_and_deny_survives (run_tests.py:891-897) passes with O_NONBLOCK removed (S_ISREG refuses the FIFO first) and with the S_ISREG check removed (O_WRONLY|O_NONBLOCK on a reader-less FIFO fails with ENXIO), so neither guard's presence is verified.
consequence: Either guard could be dropped without a test failing although the doc cites both.

title: Test runner imports scripts in-process and leaves scripts/__pycache__ behind
mechanism: test/run_tests.py:633-635 imports hdc_hooks and hdc_report in-process without sys.dont_write_bytecode, so scripts/__pycache__/*.cpython-314.pyc appear on every run (the subprocess calls already pass -B); round 5 checked for this explicitly. Gitignored, so harmless to the marketplace install.
consequence: Each test run recreates the artifact round 4/5 asked to keep out of the package.

title: 'Indicators stay out of the model's context' holds for hooks only, not the CLI
mechanism: An agent working in this repo, or any repo whose README quotes the command, can run hdc_report.py itself and read its own rate; the Goodhart rule at docs/indicators.md:53-57 is true of the hooks and Administer for the CLI.
consequence: A doc claim is unqualified; worth one sentence in the doc, not a code change.
severity: note ('worth one sentence in the doc')

title: Deny rule covers a short list of commands; doc presents it as access security and an IPL guard
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:70-80, :47 and :92 present the Edit(/.github/workflows/**) deny rule as 'a control the agent cannot talk its way past' and as what makes a required check an IPL; Claude Code Edit deny rules apply only to the edit tools, redirections and recognised commands (sed -i, tee, cp, rm, mv). Live on 2.1.291 with Bash allowed, python3 -c, sh -c, perl -pi, python3 - <<EOF, dd of=, install, truncate -s 0, ln (hard and symbolic), git rm, git mv, find -delete, xargs rm and git checkout -- all wrote to or removed workflow files; by the doc's own 'trivial variation defeats it' test (:64) the deny rule is not an IPL either.
consequence: A user who adopts the rule and reads :80 believes the shell route is closed when it is not; the doc should state coverage and bypasses and stop calling it access security.
severity: medium; fix before relying on the doc
how_found: real session (2.1.291, 15 permission sessions); read (Claude Code docs)

title: Recommended user-level pattern Edit(**/.github/workflows/**) does not cover parent directories
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:95 says the user-level rule Edit(**/.github/workflows/**) 'covers every directory'; a relative pattern is bounded by the session's working directory, so from a session started in <repo>/src it did not block Edit, echo >> or rm against ../.github/workflows/, while Edit(//**/.github/workflows/**) did; the documented absolute form is //.
consequence: A user who follows the sentence and starts a session in a package subdirectory has no rule in effect and nothing tells them.
severity: medium; fix before relying on the doc

title: Table claims Edit, Write and MultiEdit were observed; only the Edit tool was tested
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:72-79 opens 'Claude Code 2.1.289 in -p was observed' and the first row lists 'Edit, Write, MultiEdit tools', but the evidence file's step 1 tested only the Edit tool; Write is now observed (blocked under both rules on 2.1.291), MultiEdit is not and is a legacy tool.
consequence: An observation claim is stated for tools that were not observed.

title: Here-docs listed as not covered, but a here-doc into a >> redirection is blocked
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:108 lists here-docs as not covered by the deny rule; a here-doc feeding 'cat >> file' was blocked (the redirection is recognised) while a here-doc feeding 'python3 -' was not.
consequence: The 'does not cover' list is wrong for one here-doc form; the doc should say which.

title: 'Scripts that open files themselves' understates the bypass surface
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:106 names scripts as the uncovered route; plain utilities (truncate, dd, install, ln, find -delete) and a sh -c wrapper are enough (see R12).
consequence: The 'does not cover' list under-describes what passes the rule.

title: 'Documented, not observed' items are now observed and should be promoted; evidence file should gain this round's tables
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:93-97 marks the / anchor, the subdirectory case, auto-mode behaviour and sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite as documented-only; the first three were observed this round (only the sandbox item remains documentation), the .claude/settings.local.json git-root exception (since 2.1.211) is worth a clause, and the evidence file (permission-rules-2.1.289.md) lacks the 2.1.291 tables.
consequence: The doc's observed/documented status is stale.

title: 'LOPA (CCPS, 2001) is semi-quantitative' misattributes the word
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:7: the 2001 book describes itself as 'a simplified method ... between a qualitative PHA and a quantitative risk analysis'; 'semi-quantitative' is later CCPS (2012, 2016) usage.
consequence: Accurate in substance but attributed to the wrong source.

title: Integrity attribute glossed as 'probability of failure on demand'
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:7-15: the CCPS 2015 Integrity attribute is 'the risk reduction reasonably achievable by a protection layer given its design and management'; 'as a probability of failure on demand' is the doc's gloss presented as the definition, and the next section says integrity is what is being left out.
consequence: A definition is misquoted in the doc's central citation.

title: Reliability definition drops 'for a specified period of time'
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:7-15 renders Reliability as 'works as designed when called on'; the source is 'the probability that a protection layer operates according to its specification for a specified period of time'.
consequence: The time element of the definition is lost.

title: GitHub required-check section omits the if:-skipped-job and admin-bypass caveats
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:47 should add that a required job skipped by an if: condition reports Success and does not block the merge (so 'if: false' is another one-line silence), and that code-owner review binds administrators only with 'Do not allow bypassing the above settings' enabled.
consequence: Two documented ways around the required-check guard are not mentioned.

title: Independence table does not name inline suppressions
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:34-43 marks 'type checker or linter whose configuration the change does not touch' as independent, and the scenario-2 list at :28 and the 'does not cover' list at :103 name only skip/xfail markers, || true and looser assertions; # type: ignore, # noqa, # pragma: no cover, @pytest.mark.skip and eslint-disable live in the source the agent edits and silence the checker without touching its configuration.
consequence: The row claims independence that inline suppressions defeat.

title: 'A test checked against captured real output' is independent only when the capture predates the change
mechanism: docs/protection-layers.md:34-43 marks captured-output tests as independent; true for a typed accessor validated against a real API response, not for a snapshot or golden file generated from the agent's own new code, which captures the reading the test was meant to check.
consequence: The row needs the qualifier 'captured from the system before the change, or from a system the agent did not write'.

title: Rung-naming rule produces rung talk on a plain bug fix, once wrong
mechanism: With docs/CLAUDE.md in context, two of three rules-arm runs on task (b) (a plain bug fix with no remediation proposed) spent a sentence naming a rung, and one called swapping round() for Decimal 'Eliminate', which is wrong (Substitute at most); 'name the rung of every proposed fix' applied where no remediation was being proposed.
consequence: A visible cost of the older rule on ordinary fixes, worth watching as the rule set grows (accepted by design).
